pr_title: Map byte[] to json/jsonb as a raw JSON document again
pr_summary_en:
Fixes #3698

Since 10.0, a byte[] property mapped to a json/jsonb column was picked up by NpgsqlTypeMappingSource.FindCollectionMapping as a JSON primitive collection of bytes, so it was written as a JSON array of numbers and rows holding real JSON documents (e.g. written by 9.x) failed to materialize with "Invalid token type: 'StartObject'". This restores the 9.x behavior: unless an element mapping is explicitly configured (e.g. via PrimitiveCollection()), byte[] on json/jsonb falls back to NpgsqlJsonTypeMapping, which sends the bytes as the raw UTF-8 document as supported by Npgsql. The byte[] -> smallint[] and default bytea mappings are unaffected. Added type mapping unit tests and an ad-hoc functional round-trip test for both json and jsonb.
risks: (1) Behavior change for anyone who wrote data with 10.x under this mapping: those rows contain JSON arrays of numbers and will now be read back as the raw bytes of that array text (not the original bytes); this is the inverse of the current 9.x->10.x break and matches the maintainer's classification as an unintentional regression. (2) Pre-existing 9.x quirks of NpgsqlJsonTypeMapping for byte[] are unchanged: GenerateNonNullSqlLiteral sends byte[] through the 'User POCO' branch (JsonSerializer.Serialize -> base64 JSON string), so byte[] constants in SQL literals (e.g. HasData seeding, inlined constants) don't match the parameter path; GenerateCodeLiteral throws for byte[] (compiled model seed data); the default value comparer for byte[] on this mapping may not be structural, so in-place mutation of the array may not be detected (replacing the array works and is tested). Not widened to keep the change minimal. (3) Explicit PrimitiveCollection() on byte[] with jsonb keeps the 10.x collection behavior by design (tested). (4) Functional runs used PostgreSQL 16 locally; PG17/18-only tests were checked to fail identically on BASE.
